theory.title: Log vs Log To Console: When to Use Each
theory.content:
\n\n
\n\n

MENTOR-9 taps a display showing the HTML report from your last test.

Notice how you only see Log messages after opening this report? Sometimes you need real-time feedback while tests run. That's where Log To Console comes in.

Two Ways to Output Messages

Think of Robot Framework as having two communication channels:

Log - Writes to the HTML report file (log.html). You see these messages after the test finishes. Perfect for detailed records you want to review later. Like writing notes in a logbook.

Log To Console - Writes directly to your terminal/console window. You see these messages immediately as the test runs. Perfect for tracking progress in real-time. Like speaking your status updates out loud.

When to Use Each

Use Log when you want a permanent record. Variable values, detailed steps, debugging information, anything you might need to review later.

Use Log To Console when you want immediate feedback. Progress percentages, status updates, quick checks during test development.

The syntax is identical for both:

*** Test Cases ***
Diagnostic Check
    Log To Console    Starting diagnostic...
    Log               Hardware check: 47 components scanned

Using Both Together

Here's the powerful part: you can use both in the same test. Give yourself real-time progress updates in the console while building a detailed record in the log file.

*** Test Cases ***
System Scan
    Log To Console    Progress: 25%
    Log               Scanned sector A: 12 nodes found
    Log To Console    Progress: 50%
    Log               Scanned sector B: 8 nodes found
    Log To Console    Complete!

The console shows your progress ticking up. The log file has all the technical details. Best of both worlds.
